title: Pointed relative normal crossings charts and coordinate intersection ideals
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], $X$ a scheme with a morphism $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ [def-pc-scheme], $U\subseteq X$ an open subset, and $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. A relative normal crossings chart for $(f,U,\bar x)$ consists of an etale neighborhood $w:W\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], a lift of $\bar x$ to $W$, an integer $r\geq0$, and a smooth $F$-morphism $c:W\to\mathbf A_F^r$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-affine-space]. It also includes a monoid homomorphism $\mathbf N^r\to (\mathcal O_X\cap j_*\mathcal O_U^\times)(W)$, where $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, with each standard basis element mapping to the pullback of the corresponding affine coordinate. This homomorphism is a chart for the actual divisorial log structure: its induced map on every pointed geometric stalk is the chart pushout isomorphism of [def-trf-log-regular-pair]. The reduced induced closed subscheme on $W\setminus w^{-1}U$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] has ideal sheaf equal to the ideal generated by the product of those pulled-back coordinates [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. For a subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$, define the intersection ideal of the corresponding coordinate branches to be the quasi-coherent ideal sheaf generated by $c^*z_i$ for $i\in S$. Its associated closed subscheme is their scheme-theoretic intersection. The empty subset gives the zero ideal and the whole neighborhood. Rank zero is allowed: the product is $1$ and the boundary is empty. The definition does not require all coordinate branches to pass through the chosen point; this is a separate possible property of a chart. No existence of a chart is asserted.
